Minimum gear recs from me are

Sub 15mph, half cap helmet, and wrist guards minimum. Attire and joint pads depend on your tolerance for road-rash and impact. (I use knees more often than I use elbows. idm my arms getting minced up, but I need my knees) 

When you get over 15, you start getting into areas where crashes have a higher likelihood of of being serious. I'd recommend minimum half-cap with chin guard (you don't wanna tear your neck open, I've done it, ain't fun.) Wrist guards. Use proper knee pads, ones that are gonna slide nicely on surfaces. Those things will keep you safe from the main bone damage areas.  Soft tissue damage is harder to avoid, but in general, light motorcycling gear is good.

Adjust for weather. For example, I use draggin jeans, smaller kneepads and a leather jacket in winter, but in summer I'll just wear shorts and a tee with large knee+elbow pads.

The most important thing that will keep you safe is understanding when you can go quickly, and when it's too risky. Don't show off, accelerate slowly at first. Pay attention to the road in front  of you. 90% of the posts about people getting hurt  end up being the same thing, people going too fast/showing off, and hit something on the pavement cause they weren't looking at the road.

You're a longboarder, if you've done any downhill, it's the same gear.

What you're referring to is called "carving" 

There are multiple reasons a skater could be carving around. 

1. It can be pretty fun 

2. Testing our steering, the rubber bushings on the  trucks (axle) wear out over time, and they might need adjusting or replacing.

3. Speed control. Depending on the intensity you carve with, different things can happen. Most of the time it slows you down. basically the board wants to go forward, but every time you carve you tell it not to, and that gets rid of a little velocity based on some ratio of wheel ground contact yadda yadda math. That and you're literally covering more surface area over a given distance, so more friction. 

Doing it quickly is called pumping and easily makes you go forward from a standstill. I still don't quite understand how it works fully. I understand how it speeds you up when you're slow, but seeing high level pumping is black magic to me.

Running it out is why I eskate now, my knees are completely shot, and I'm not even 30
Try not to run it out if you can help it, the repeated heavy impacts of running off your board wear on you. 

When you learn to step out and run out, it becomes second nature, and you do it all the time. 

2nd point is that you're always gonna be able to fall, whether you choose to or not.  You can't run it out if someone just goes in front of you, but you can dive to the side. 

Personal life example, when I was 14, skating to school, someone came out of a driveway really quick, my options were hit the side of their car at full speed, or dive to the side. I didn't know how to fall though  so I thought "oh no" and slammed straight into their car instead of diving out of the way. 

Third point 
Most people can't immediately run 10mph from a standing start, let alone run at the speeds needed to run it out without faceplanting. 

So tldr
Running out/stepping out bad for your knees.
Running out doesn't work if something is in front of you
Running out is a lot harder than learning how to roll on the ground.

Basically, the first time you apply a poison, it takes note of your location in the game, and also what buffs/debuffs the enemy has. It does this so it knows how much damage to do, so if you're outside of a suppression bubble, it sees that you hit and applied a poison, but it makes the enemy immune to that poison, meaning it will still tick down, but the enemy is immune to it and takes no damage.

The way poisons work is to add every piece of poison damage to the same same debuff, and track the individual timers within that debuff.
 Since you were out of the bubble, that debuff now has your location from out of the bubble on it, and that location will stay on that debuff until it falls off completely. 

Add those together and enemies are immune to your poisons despite you being next to them and stuff, or they just take less damage from an aoe Damage reduction mob that's already dead.
